name: Occasional Mental Factors
intro: Six factors that arise in some mind-moments but not all, and that can serve either wholesome or unwholesome ends. Four came with the jhāna factors and the bojjhaṅgas; two are new.

words.gloss: decision; resolve that settles on the object

etymology.note: the mind letting go of wavering and landing — the opposite pole of vicikicchā

words.gloss: desire-to-act; wish, zeal for the object

etymology.note: ethically neutral wanting — the same factor drives kāmacchanda and the first iddhipāda

talk.text: places the mind on the object and
is the wish to do — which, pointed at
, becomes a base of power, and pointed at sense pleasure becomes a hindrance.

suttaRec.title: Anupada — One by One as They Occurred
suttaRec.blurb: Sāriputta reviews each jhāna factor by factor as it arises — the suttas' own list of mental factors, the seed of the Abhidhamma chart.
